channel.title: Wire — Frontend
channel.description: Frontend from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: CSS-Tricks has a new owner
item.description: Yes, I've got the keys to the castle, so to speak. And, even after 12 years of working on the site, I'll admit I'm a little overwhelmed and nervous about that. (4 sources: frontendfocus, hackernews, javascriptweekly, lobsters)

item.title: Safari 27.1 previews the Device Posture and Viewport Segments APIs
item.description: Today iPhone Duo arrives, and with it, Safari 27.1. (2 sources: frontendfocus, javascriptweekly)

item.title: Websites Should Be Printable
item.description: A place for the personal blog, projects, and wanderings of Brennen Puth. (2 sources: frontendfocus, lobsters)

item.title: Would You Let Your AI Agent Grade Its Own Homework?
item.description: Meticulous auto-generates and auto-maintains visual frontend browser tests, providing a level of coverage that is unattainable with manually written tests. (2 sources: frontendfocus, javascriptweekly)

item.title: Building an Isolated Preview for AI-Generated HTML
item.description: An iframe with srcdoc feels like a safe place to render HTML a model wrote. It isn't. Three tests show how the preview can read your page, escape the frame, and phone home, and four layers of protection close each hole. (2 sources: frontendfocus, javascriptweekly)

item.title: HTML-in-Canvas: Interactive DOM Inside 2D, WebGL and WebGPU Canvases
item.description: Chrome 157 ships the HTML-in-Canvas API, letting you render live, interactive, and accessible DOM subtrees into 2D, WebGL, and WebGPU canvases. (1 source: frontendfocus)
